neighborhood_overview:
PÈRE LACHAISE CEMETERY
The Père-Lachaise Cemetery is probably the most famous cemetery in Paris, if not the world. And you can understand why when you visit it. Although Paris is full of attractive cemeteries (Montparnasse, Montmartre, Batignolles), this one is the most surprising, and the most beautiful, by many aspects.
First of all, of course, because it welcomes a tremendous amount of celebrities from all over the world. But also because during your walk in its paved streets, you will discover a great number of plant species, something that one does not necessarily expect to find here. Cherry trees, maples, chestnut trees, weeping willows, walnut trees... The Père-Lachaise cemetery has about 5000 trees representing about 50 different species spread over an area of 44 hectares. This makes the place the largest green space in Paris!
Not to be missed during your visit:
The tomb of Allan Kardec, founder of spiritualism, whose grave, the most flowered in the cemetery

neighborhood_overview: Le Marais, located on the right bank of the Seine in Paris, is a historic district rich in heritage and culture. This district was founded in the Middle Ages, and its name, meaning "swamp" in French, reflects its humid origins. From the 16th century, it became a residential area popular with the French nobility, marked by the construction of many sumptuous mansions such as the Hôtel de Sully and the Hôtel Carnavalet. The Marais has retained its old-world charm, with cobbled alleys, secret inner courtyards and hidden gardens. Today, it is one of the most trendy and cosmopolitan districts in Paris, attracting both Parisians and tourists. The Place des Vosges, one of the oldest and most beautiful squares in Paris, is the beating heart, surrounded by elegant arcades and red brick buildings. The area has also been home to a vibrant Jewish community for centuries, concentrated around rue des Rosiers, where you’ll find synagogues, bakeries and kosher restaurants.

Je suis gestionnaire de propriétés privées en location de courte & moyenne durée depuis 2016 à Paris, sur la côte basque et la côte d'azur.. 

Passionnée, curieuse, gourmande, énergique...des mots qui me décrivent à la perfection!

Mes passions: 
La culture & l'Art. Mon précédent métier d'Agent d'Artistes m'a permis d'admirer des trésors inestimables, de découvrir une richesse incomparable dans le domaine de la création en France.

La cuisine. Je dois cette passion pour à ma grand mère. J'ai même eu ma chance dans l'émission Un dîner presque parfait en 2014 ;-). Aujourd'hui c'est avec mes filles que je passe du temps aux fourneaux. Le bonheur!

Le sport. Le jogging, comment dire? C'est mon défouloir! Surtout le long de l'Océan à Anglet!

Les sorties. J'aime Paris pour ça! Théâtre, expositions, concerts, spectacles, restaurants, bars, balades. Les sorties sont à couper le souffle à Paris tellement le choix est vaste. Il en existe pour tout le monde. Amoureux, célibataire, papi et mamie, enfants, animaux, bref, impossible de s'ennuyer! 
J'adore le quartier Saint Germain-des-prés, ses terrasses, ses galeries, ses boutiques, ses librairies, son histoire. 
J'adore aussi me balader à Montmartre, quartier le plus visité de Paris. La butte Montmartre est célèbre pour sa Basilique du Sacré Cœur et sa vue panoramique sur Paris. C'est aussi un quartier gastronomique et culturel au charme authentique, parsemé d'escaliers et de vieux lampadaires. Prenez le petit train de Montmartre depuis la place Blanche. C'est très sympa à faire en famille.

Chers voyageurs, sachez que vous êtes les bienvenus, à Paris, sur la Côte Basque ou en région PACA. Vous serez accueillis avec soin par moi même ou par mon équipe. Tout dépend où je me trouve ;-).

Les logements que je propose à la location saisonnière sont tous très bien équipés pour un confort optimal. C'est très important pour moi que vous gardiez un bon souvenir de vos vacances ou séjours professionnels.

Je vous souhaite un très beau moment, chez nous.

Delphine Thomas
SAS Thomas Real Estate

neighborhood_overview:
Montmartre is a historical parisian neighborhood, it is altogether dynamic, fun, and full of monuments and charm. The old part of the neighborhood, when climbing the hill towards place du Tertre and the Sacré-Coeur, has an artistic tradition and still hosts many painters. It is truly romantic and the panoramas are gorgeous from up there. But it's also a great neighborhood to party: a lot of bars stay open very late at night, and you'll find many clubs.
The gardens of Sacre Coeur are two minutes away, Montmartre is the ideal place for resting after visiting "le grand Paris". Public transportations and shopping streets like Rue des Abbesses and rue des Martyrs are very close, suitable for a family or group of friends visiting the city!

The 5th arrondissement of Paris (also known as "arrondissement du Panthéon") is one of the 20 arrondissements (administrative districts) of the capital city of France.

- Sanitise their mobile phones

Located in the historic heart of Paris, the Marais neighborhood was once a marshy area before becoming one of the most cosmopolitan and fashionable neighborhoods in the capital.


As a result of the construction of Place Royale (the current Place des Vosges), the area has begun to attract people from wealthy social classes, who have built sumptuous mansions and mansions. Nowadays, it is possible to visit some of these buildings, converted into museums, such as the Carnavalet Museum, the Picasso Museum, the Cognacq-Jay Museum or the Victor Hugo House.

This historic area is largely residential in character, with many Haussmann-style mansions that have been carved into apartment buildings. The district is noted for high-end restaurants like Le Relais d'Auteuil where diners can experience French haute-cuisine at its best. Auteuil is located just east of the southwest corner of the Bois de Boulogne, which is perfect for a picnic or a lunchtime stroll. neighborhood_overview:
Paris’ "Grands Boulevards" district is legendary for its old-world style and cosmopolitanism. Originally comprising the wide network of roads that span from the Madeleine church in the 9th arrondissement to Bastille in the 11th arrondissement, the opening of the Grands Boulevards metro station in 1998 means the area has since been mostly associated with the enormous street stretching between the Metro stations Bonne Nouvelle and Richelieu Drouot.


Dotted with countless theaters, clubs and cafes, the boulevards’ wide sidewalks are perfect for people-watching, strolling and leisurely nursing cafés crèmes on heated terraces. Browsing the nearby 19th century "arcades", or covered passageways, is a must for shoppers looking for that authentic and chic Parisian gift. The area, seemingly timeless, still remains impossibly steeped in the turn-of-the-century urban glamour that made it famous in the first place.

Here, I know every street, café, restaurant, club, and all good address in this wonderful neighbourhood, the most pleasant in Paris : La Louisiane stand exactly in the middle. The hotel has always preserved with humbleness the authentic and poetic spirit of “The Quartier" in its rooms. And it still organize its artistic and literary events, far from luxury boutiques and snobbish places.
To read more about the hotel and its district last news and lifestyle reviews, and discover our last pictures,  you may go to our social network page HotelLaLouisiane : our publications are in French but you may use automatic translation tools.

About me : literature enthusiast, art lover, history buff, boardgames player, runner (marathon level), and also globetrotter. Journalist at start and then Internet pioneer in the 1990’s & serial startups founder, I'm now dedicated to the Hotel La Louisiane like my ancestors : I am the 4th owner of my family in a row. La Louisiane is an historical place of Saint-Germain-des-Prés since year Thousand eight hundred and twenty-three (1823). The foundations of the hotel date back to the Roman Empire, and the oldest part to the 15th century. Here we host since two centuries travellers, writers, artists, musicians, entrepreneurs and of course travellers from 119 different countries.
Advertising La Louisiane via AirBnB is first of all a chance to meet with people from all over the world to appreciate cultural diversity : every year, travelers from all continents meet here, in a cosmopolitan and friendly atmosphere.

name: Luxury one bedroom, Heart of Marais
description:
Lovely 1 bedroom apartment - floor area 62m² 2nd floor. Sleeps 4.
In the heart of Marais, steps from Place des Vosges, metro Hotel de Ville.
Quiet king bedroom overlooking the courtyard. Charming kitchenette. Marble shower and separate bath. High ceilings.
neighborhood_overview: Our neighborhood is the "real" Paris, and is a favorite of Parisians because of its many secret gardens and delicious pastry and bread shops. It is minutes by foot to Notre Dame, the Louvre, Place des Vosges, and is on the central metro line in the heart of the city.
host_about:
We are a professional couple that love to share our homes in London and Paris with fellow lovers of travel. 

For London:
Our favorite things to do include walking to the end of our street and out onto Victoria Embankment Gardens to see the Thames and enjoy a book on the lawns. 
Also short walk from the home is St. James Park with swans, wild green parrots, and squirrels which will gently take nuts from your hand. 
The Churchill War Rooms is a museum not to be missed. They do an incredible job of bringing the courage of the British during WWII, to life. 
You may hop on the Uber boat at Embankment and enjoy a ride to the doorstep of the Tower of London Palace to see the Crown jewels and take a tour with the guards who live on the palace grounds.  
For Paris:
Our favorite things include visiting a different hidden garden in our neighborhood for a picnic. We are still discovering new places! 
We enjoy visiting the Louvre on the weekend afternoons, a 15 minute walk. 
In the evenings we like to listen to the free concerts at Place des Vosges, a 4 minute walk from our home. 
Bertillon is our favorite place for ice cream and is a 7 minute walk. Enjoy it at night in front of the beautifully lit Notre Dame. 
We are spoiled for good restaurants immediately outside our doorstep, and art such as the amazing Picasso museum is a short stroll. I hope you enjoy staying at our home, and visit again and again.

Je suis gestionnaire de propriétés privées en location de courte & moyenne durée depuis 2016 à Paris, sur la côte basque et la côte d'azur.. 

Passionnée, curieuse, gourmande, énergique...des mots qui me décrivent à la perfection!

Mes passions: 
La culture & l'Art. Mon précédent métier d'Agent d'Artistes m'a permis d'admirer des trésors inestimables, de découvrir une richesse incomparable dans le domaine de la création en France.

La cuisine. Je dois cette passion pour à ma grand mère. J'ai même eu ma chance dans l'émission Un dîner presque parfait en 2014 ;-). Aujourd'hui c'est avec mes filles que je passe du temps aux fourneaux. Le bonheur!

Le sport. Le jogging, comment dire? C'est mon défouloir! Surtout le long de l'Océan à Anglet!

Les sorties. J'aime Paris pour ça! Théâtre, expositions, concerts, spectacles, restaurants, bars, balades. Les sorties sont à couper le souffle à Paris tellement le choix est vaste. Il en existe pour tout le monde. Amoureux, célibataire, papi et mamie, enfants, animaux, bref, impossible de s'ennuyer! 
J'adore le quartier Saint Germain-des-prés, ses terrasses, ses galeries, ses boutiques, ses librairies, son histoire. 
J'adore aussi me balader à Montmartre, quartier le plus visité de Paris. La butte Montmartre est célèbre pour sa Basilique du Sacré Cœur et sa vue panoramique sur Paris. C'est aussi un quartier gastronomique et culturel au charme authentique, parsemé d'escaliers et de vieux lampadaires. Prenez le petit train de Montmartre depuis la place Blanche. C'est très sympa à faire en famille.

Chers voyageurs, sachez que vous êtes les bienvenus, à Paris, sur la Côte Basque ou en région PACA. Vous serez accueillis avec soin par moi même ou par mon équipe. Tout dépend où je me trouve ;-).

Les logements que je propose à la location saisonnière sont tous très bien équipés pour un confort optimal. C'est très important pour moi que vous gardiez un bon souvenir de vos vacances ou séjours professionnels.

Je vous souhaite un très beau moment, chez nous.

Delphine Thomas
SAS Thomas Real Estate

PLACE DE LA BOURSE:
The Bourse district is known for being a fashion hotspot. In the past, young women rushed to buy jewelry and lace. Today, trendy designers have invaded the surrounding area, like Kenzo, Thierry Muggler, Cacharel, Agatha... Place des Victoires is surrounded by buildings and mansions, representative of 19th century Parisian elegance. As evening falls, the facades light up and the square takes on the romantic air of Paris in the 1920s.

Close to the Grands Boulevards of Paris, the Bourse district is appreciated for its calm and typical Parisian atmosphere. It is a neighborhood mainly frequented by businessmen and Parisian bobos, where it is easy to find a pleasant place for lunch.
Opened in 1686, the Place des Victoires was the first place built in honor of the King of the Sun. At the time, a 7-meter-high statue, crowned with Louis XIV rising in the center of the square. It was replaced in 1822 by the current statue of Louis XIV on horseback.

host_about:
My name is Cristina, I grew up in sunny Madrid, Spain and have been living in Paris for the last 20 years. I've also spent short periods of time living in Italy and California. 

I'm married to Matteo, a wonderful Italian man, whom I adore and want to grow old with. He is an engineer and digital entrepreneur. He loves scuba-diving and running marathons, and I believe he has some magical power that makes children and animals always so comfortable around him!

On my side, I love long walks, cooking, reading in a lazy Sunday afternoon just  to relax and spending time with the lovely people in my life doing anything that seems fun. 
Work-wise I was a designer for 10 years in the tech industry. 
Some years ago I decided to focus on my art practice and I now have my own studio. My work combines painting and drawing with electronics performance and installations.

Matteo and I are an incurable optimists, and you'll see us smiling more often than not. We highly value honesty, respect, tolerance and courage. We enjoy being with people and are very sociable (We both speak fluent English, Spanish, Italian and French which helps when travelling) though we also relish and understand the need for moments of quietness and solitude. 

When we travel we avoid doing crazy kodak-moment tourism. We'd rather see less cities or monuments and try to stay enough time in one place, so we  can get a feel of it and what it has to offer and how people live there.

In 2011 we tried Airbnb for a business trip to San Francisco and have never looked back to hotels. We decided to renovate a little studio on top of our apartment. Since then have been the lucky hosts of many wonderful guests, we love meeting so many people from all over the world and feel lucky to belong to such a special community!

neighborhood_overview:
Located in the 10th arrondissement of Paris, the Porte-Saint-Martin district is a real hidden treasure. Bounded by rue des Récollets to the north, boulevard Saint-Martin, place de la République and rue du Faubourg-du-Temple to the south, it offers a unique blend of culture and history. The district, once crossed by a branch of the Seine, has evolved into a dynamic urban area protected by an enclosure designed by Charles V. Visitors can explore the Church of Saint-Laurent, a historic monument in neo-Gothic style, and the Porte Saint-Martin, a triumphal arch erected in 1674 in honor of Louis XIV's victories. The Canal Saint-Martin, inaugurated in 1825, adds a picturesque touch, linking the Bassin de la Villette to the Port de l'Arsenal and once supplying the city with drinking water. The Place de la République, with its statue of Marianne, is a veritable communications hub.

The Porte-Saint-Martin district is packed with points of interest and green spaces perfect for relaxing.

neighborhood_overview: Come discover one of the Paris' up-and-coming neighbourhoods, the Goutte d’Or, which is coming to fulfil the promise of its name (golden drop). The Goutte d'Or boasts delicious coffee, a lively market, and surprising perspectives on the Sacré-Coeur. BBC Travel also called it "the emerging design hub of Paris", with young jewellery and fashion designers setting up shop next to textile workshops, fashion and accessories boutiques, makers of leather goods and upmarket furniture (Maison Chateau Rouge, Daigremont...).

host_about:
Greetings from the Veeve team!


Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods. Thanks to our fully managed service, when you stay in a Veeve property you can benefit from the spaciousness, personal style and relaxed feel of a home – but with all the amenities of a hotel.


Once a booking is confirmed our Customer Service team will become your main point of contact and get in touch with you to organise your arrival at the property (including airport transfers, upon request); after which our on-the-ground management team will look after all aspects of your stay, with in-stay support available to help with any queries.


We have strict cleanliness guidelines for our cleaners and all staff who enter our properties and have reinforced existing cleaning procedures in line with official WHO, British and French government guidance.


As always, our team ensure that all properties are cleaned to a professional standard before and after each stay, with increased focus on touch-point cleaning (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.).

 All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:

Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods.  All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate
- Wash and disinfect work shoes


We might be able to arrange for property viewings, upon request, for stays of over 28 nights. 

Please be aware once a booking is confirmed you will be required to complete a Rental Agreement and also  ID verification via our partners Superhog. This is mandatory for all our stays and in accordance to short lets requirements with Veeve.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be sure to answer you promptly.

Martin-Luther King Park is the highlight. Covering an area of 10 hectares, this wild paradise imagined by landscaper Jacqueline Osty is designed around three themes: water, sport, and the seasons. The park also gave birth to two shared gardens committed to ecology

Greetings from the Veeve team!


Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods. We have strict cleanliness guidelines for our cleaners and all staff who enter our properties and have reinforced existing cleaning procedures in line with official WHO, British and French government guidance.


As always, our team ensure that all properties are cleaned to a professional standard before and after each stay, with increased focus on touch-point cleaning (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.).

 All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate
- Wash and disinfect work shoes


We might be able to arrange for property viewings, upon request, for stays of over 28 nights. 

Please be aware once a booking is confirmed you will be required to complete a Rental Agreement and also  ID verification via our partners Superhog. This is mandatory for all our stays and in accordance to short lets requirements with Veeve.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be sure to answer you promptly.

The neighborhood was the home of thousands of artists and writers, many of whom were expatriates, during the 1920s and 1930s, the postwar period referred to as Les Années Folles. Today the area is far more upscale in nature, with boutique hotels and gourmet grocery stores. You can also dine at La Closerie Des Lilas, one of Ernest Hemingway's old watering holes. The neighborhood is served by Paris's 4, 6, and 13 Metro lines.

The Marais is a multicultural, historic neighborhood bursting with life. It's a place of encounters and contrasts. On one side, cobbled streets and private mansions recall the Paris of yesteryear; on the other, trendy boutiques and lively cafés embody modernity. Parisians and tourists meet in this unique place, where the Parisian art of living blends with a cosmopolitan atmosphere.

The trendy Marais district is also brimming with world-renowned historic monuments. Among the emblematic buildings that dot the district, the majestic Place des Vosges stands out for its classical architecture and peaceful gardens. This landscape offers a welcome retreat from the hustle and bustle of the city.

This arrondissement, without any major sites, is a story of two tales; to   north-eastern end of the 17th, more commonly known as Batignolles, you’ll   find a relaxed bohemian atmosphere with a large variety of bars and eateries. host_about:
Greetings from the Veeve team!


Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods. Thanks to our fully managed service, when you stay in a Veeve property you can benefit from the spaciousness, personal style and relaxed feel of a home – but with all the amenities of a hotel.


Once a booking is confirmed our Customer Service team will become your main point of contact and get in touch with you to organise your arrival at the property (including airport transfers, upon request); after which our on-the-ground management team will look after all aspects of your stay, with in-stay support available to help with any queries.


We have strict cleanliness guidelines for our cleaners and all staff who enter our properties and have reinforced existing cleaning procedures in line with official WHO, British and French government guidance.


As always, our team ensure that all properties are cleaned to a professional standard before and after each stay, with increased focus on touch-point cleaning (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.).

 All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate
- Wash and disinfect work shoes


We might be able to arrange for property viewings, upon request, for stays of over 28 nights. 

Please be aware once a booking is confirmed you will be required to complete a Rental Agreement and also  ID verification via our partners Superhog. This is mandatory for all our stays and in accordance to short lets requirements with Veeve.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be sure to answer you promptly.

Bienvenue à La Villa Flore!
La Villa Flore est une charmante chaumière avec jardin en Normandie à 450 m de la mer. 
Tout proche d’Étretat, à 5 km à vol d'oiseau. 
Un petit nid douillet, situé à Saint Jouin Bruneval, au coeur d'un site historique classé : "La Valleuse de Bruneval"
Un hameau d'époque, un havre de paix, un petit coin de paradis! 
La Villa Flore est très calme, si vous avez besoin de bien vous reposer, c'est le lieu idéal! Verdoyant, ressourçant!!!
Et les délicieux plateaux de fruits de mer à emporter sont à 2 pas ;-)!
De belles ballades sur les falaises ou dans la forêt s'offrent à vous. 
À 5 min en voiture de la plage de sable et de galets de Saint Jouin Bruneval vous pourrez y découvrir beaucoup d'activités différentes l'été : 
le Jetski, la voile, le catamaran, le kite surf, le padle, le flyboard, le char à voile, la natation, les promenades en bord de mer à pied ou à cheval, dans la nature, la cabane de lecture où vos enfants auront gratuitement accès aux livres, la plaine de jeu, les douches de plages le long des magnifiques falaises. 
Vous êtes également à 15 min de la piscine de Criquetot L'Esneval, avec son Sauna, Hammam, Jacuzzi , courant, tobbogan, bain chaud, salle de sport et bowling. 
Vous dégusterez les spécialités de la région dans les restaurants de plage très accueillants avec leurs belles terrasses ensoleillées et leurs parasols.
Les balades sur les falaises offre une vue splendide sur la mer. Il y a beaucoup de plage différentes à découvrir près de La Villa Flore et notamment la célèbre plage d'Étretat avec son aiguille creuse qui plonge dans une mer émeraude souvent peinte par Claude Monet.
Description de La Villa Flore :
Une villa confortable pour 4/5 personnes + lit parapluie de bébé + 1 berceau.
Au rez de chaussée : 
1 grande pièce ouverte : Salon, salle à manger avec son poêle à bois, chauffage électrique, table 10/12 personnes, connection internet wi-fi, TV, 2 chaises hautes pour bébé.
Cuisine américaine très bien équipée pour amateurs de bonne cuisine :
Réfrigérateur, congélateur, four, plaque vitrocéramiques, gaz, lave-vaisselle.
Arrière cuisine :
Lave linge, sèche linge, micro-onde, congélateur, planche à repasser, fer à repasser, étendoir.
Au premier étage : 
Deux chambres spacieuses: 
Chambre 'Libellule' avec sa salle de bain: 'Bulle de savon' et Chambre 'Coccinelle'.
Écran plat, lecteur DVD, lit parapluie bébé, berceau, petit bain pour bébé, porte bébé pour les balades.
Joli jardin avec plantes aromatiques...
Et parking pour la voiture dans l'enceinte de la propriété.
Gîte Non fumeur.
Séjour heureux garanti ;-)!
A très bientôt!
Laurence

Hello, my name is Xavier. Since now 52 years, I'm a true "Germanopratin". I was born here in Saint-Germain-des-Prés, where I have always lived. Here, I know every street, café, restaurant, club, and all good address in this wonderful neighbourhood, the most pleasant in Paris : La Louisiane stand exactly in the middle. The hotel has always preserved with humbleness the authentic and poetic spirit of “The Quartier" in its rooms. And it still organize its artistic and literary events, far from luxury boutiques and snobbish places.
To read more about the hotel and its district last news and lifestyle reviews, and discover our last pictures,  you may go to our social network page HotelLaLouisiane : our publications are in French but you may use automatic translation tools.
La Louisiane team do its best to give to our guests the best conditions to stay in Saint-Germain des Prés and Paris left bank, called the Latin Quarter.  My cohosts are Jacek, Alexandra, Charlotte, Antoine, Cyprien and Philippe.
About me : literature enthusiast, art lover, history buff, boardgames player, runner (marathon level), and also globetrotter. Journalist at start and then Internet pioneer in the 1990’s & serial startups founder, I'm now dedicated to the Hotel La Louisiane like my ancestors : I am the 4th owner of my family in a row. La Louisiane is an historical place of Saint-Germain-des-Prés since year Thousand eight hundred and twenty-three (1823). The foundations of the hotel date back to the Roman Empire, and the oldest part to the 15th century. Here we host since two centuries travellers, writers, artists, musicians, entrepreneurs and of course travellers from 119 different countries.
Advertising La Louisiane via AirBnB is first of all a chance to meet with people from all over the world to appreciate cultural diversity : every year, travelers from all continents meet here, in a cosmopolitan and friendly atmosphere.
Looking forward to meeting with you soon in the nicest district of Paris, in the heart of Saint-Germain des Prés, and to helping you enjoy an unforgettable experience!

host_about:
Greetings from the Veeve team!


Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods. Thanks to our fully managed service, when you stay in a Veeve property you can benefit from the spaciousness, personal style and relaxed feel of a home – but with all the amenities of a hotel.


Once a booking is confirmed our Customer Service team will become your main point of contact and get in touch with you to organise your arrival at the property (including airport transfers, upon request); after which our on-the-ground management team will look after all aspects of your stay, with in-stay support available to help with any queries.


We have strict cleanliness guidelines for our cleaners and all staff who enter our properties and have reinforced existing cleaning procedures in line with official WHO, British and French government guidance.


As always, our team ensure that all properties are cleaned to a professional standard before and after each stay, with increased focus on touch-point cleaning (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.).

 All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate
- Wash and disinfect work shoes


We might be able to arrange for property viewings, upon request, for stays of over 28 nights. 

Please be aware once a booking is confirmed you will be required to complete a Rental Agreement and also  ID verification via our partners Superhog. This is mandatory for all our stays and in accordance to short lets requirements with Veeve.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be sure to answer you promptly.

A glance at some of the beautiful buildings and houses indicates the wealthy status of the former residents. After the revolution, much of the area was abandoned by the rich, and poor bohemian types moved in. (almost the opposite of Soho in NY) The area was considered so squalid at this point it was nearly destroyed by city officials who wanted to modernize Paris. (A huge avenue cutting through the center of the Marais was only avoided by the start of WWI.) You should keep in mind that before Napoleon showed up the Marais is what most of Paris looked like--- a labyrinth of cobblestone alleys. The rest of Paris was razed by Napoleon and Haussman who wanted to build huge avenues and gigantic squares such as the Place Concorde. name: Charming Guest Room in Butte aux Cailles
description:
Welcome to our charming home located in the picturesque neighborhood of Butte aux Cailles, one of Paris's best-kept secrets. Nestled on the second floor, you will find a cozy haven at Irène's, where authenticity and charm combine for an unforgettable Parisian experience.

You will be welcomed by two comfortable bedrooms, each equipped with two single beds and a bathroom, perfect for two friends or a family traveling in Paris.
neighborhood_overview:
The Butte aux Cailles is located in the 13th arrondissement of Paris, between Place d'Italie and Parc Montsouris. This neighborhood, with its village-like atmosphere, charms walkers who explore its narrow streets and cobblestone roads lined with small, flower-adorned houses. Notable examples include Rue Alphand, Passage Barrault, Passage Sigaud, and the charming Rue Michal.

The Petite Alsace - a worker's estate opened in 1913 with around forty small half-timbered houses - and the beautifully flowered Villa Daviel are must-sees in the area. The Art Deco swimming pool of the Butte aux Cailles is one of the neighborhood's landmarks. The vibrant Rue des Cinq Diamants is filled with numerous local shops and restaurants.

Additionally, one can discover many murals by the artist Miss.Tic throughout the area.

description:
The hotel Romance Malesherbes welcomes you in a refined and elegant setting inspired by Romanticism, a cultural movement of the late 18th and early 19th century.
You will stay in a quiet street in the 17th arrondissement of Paris, in one of our carefully decorated rooms, a few minutes from the Champs-Élysées, Montmartre and Parc Monceau.

neighborhood_overview:
The 17th arrondissement of Paris is not well known for its cultural aspect, but it offers many possibilities, both classic and original. We are pleased to share them with you:

Marché de Lévis: One of the most beautiful markets in the capital. In the past, it was a political meeting place frequented by famous people such as Victor Hugo or Auguste Blanqui. Today, this place is home to fruit and vegetable vendors, worthy of the most beautiful markets in Provence. Come and meet the craftsmen, an opportunity to discover local life in a different way! Rue de Lévis, 75017 Paris.

Musée Cernuschi: Henri Cernuschi was a humanist financier who set out to discover Asia in 1871. He brought back unique collections of Far Eastern art objects, which he bequeathed to the city of Paris in 1896. The Cernuschi Museum now exhibits all these treasures, which will undoubtedly surprise you! 7 avenue Vélasquez. Open from 10am to 5.40pm. Closed on Mondays and public holidays.

host_about:
Jeune diplomée, ayant beaucoup voyagée, je suis sociable et souriante.
J'adore la musique et les soirées comme toutes les filles de mon age :) 
- TODOLIST : Il y a un super italien (Dolce Romana) un peu plus haut dans la rue et Plus bas vous trouverez Mouffetard, district atypic conservé, une succession de petites rues piétonnes avec de bons restaurants et surtout la nuit venant le quartier devient très animée avec des pintes à 4€ :)
A moins de 10 minutes vous retrouverez le QG de la graffeuse Mistic, le fameux mais non des moindres : La Butte aux cailles. Nov 6, 2015 - A l'origine, la Butte-aux-Cailles était une petite colline plantée de moulins à vent à flancs de coteaux. Aujourd'hui, bien que les prairies et les bois aient fait place aux venelles pavées, elle demeure un paisible faubourg en marge de l'agitation parisienne. Préservée de la folie architecturale, "la Butte" comme on l'appelle a su garder son âme de village. Un lieu idéal pour se balader, ou diner en famille ou avec des amis.


J'espère que vous aimerez mon p'tit coin cosy, on s'y sent très bien et le métro est LITTÉRALEMENT en bas. Vous aurez droit au soleil pour vous réveiller (sauf si vous baissez les volets électriques) mais malheureusement à Paris il n'y a pas les petits oiseaux ^^ Seulement des pigeons !

Profitez, souriez et baladez vous bien dans cette belle ville remplie d'une culture historique :)

- Sanitise their mobile phones

Greetings from the Veeve team!


Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods. Thanks to our fully managed service, when you stay in a Veeve property you can benefit from the spaciousness, personal style and relaxed feel of a home – but with all the amenities of a hotel.


Once a booking is confirmed our Customer Service team will become your main point of contact and get in touch with you to organise your arrival at the property (including airport transfers, upon request); after which our on-the-ground management team will look after all aspects of your stay, with in-stay support available to help with any queries.


We have strict cleanliness guidelines for our cleaners and all staff who enter our properties and have reinforced existing cleaning procedures in line with official WHO, British and French government guidance.


As always, our team ensure that all properties are cleaned to a professional standard before and after each stay, with increased focus on touch-point cleaning (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.).

 All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate
- Wash and disinfect work shoes


We might be able to arrange for property viewings, upon request, for stays of over 28 nights. 

Please be aware once a booking is confirmed you will be required to complete a Rental Agreement and also  ID verification via our partners Superhog. This is mandatory for all our stays and in accordance to short lets requirements with Veeve.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be sure to answer you promptly.

neighborhood_overview:
The 1st arrondissement of Paris is a true gem in the heart of the French capital, steeped in history and culture, and bursting with points of interest for both tourists and professionals.
At the center of this district are :
- The famous Louvre Museum, one of the largest and most prestigious art museums in the world.
- The Tuileries Garden, a magnificent public park dating back to the 16th century, where visitors can stroll among shaded alleys, admire classical sculptures, and enjoy breathtaking views of the Place de la Concorde and the Arc de Triomphe.
- Not far from there, the Châtelet-les-Halles district is a true cultural and commercial hub, housing theaters, cinemas, restaurants, shops, and the famous Centre Pompidou, a contemporary art center renowned for its exceptional collection and temporary exhibitions.

The 1st arrondissement is also Paris's business district, home to many financial institutions, corporate headquarters, and government offices.

host_about:
I'm an Australian from Sydney, now living in Paris. I am alternately a bookseller, publisher, editor and book coach. Sometimes I get carried away and introduce myself as a writer. When I travel, I love discovering new towns and cities on foot, getting to know them at street level. And when my feet get sore, I'll often be found resting them in a sunny cafe, or in a quiet corner of a gallery, with a notebook and pen, just watching the world go by. 

I'm the guy who reads all the information on every exhibit in the museum. My friends know just to keep walking, and wait for me in the museum bookshop at the end. Then I spend hours in the bookshop too! In fact, I spend a lot of time in bookshops anywhere I go -- such wonderful places, bookshops. I work with eBooks in my job, but I still personally prefer print -- especially when I'm travelling.

I have been guilty of taking photos of my food. And wine labels. I know, I'm one of those people. 

Outside of the cities, I love a good road trip, stopping off in little towns and villages, or taking impromptu detours to visit a cellar door, or a scenic lookout. My parents run their own B&B in a town on the Murray River, and when I travel I love to stay in B&B's wherever possible -- it's so much more personal, and genuine. I'm also just as happy camping. I spent most of my childhood tramping around the Australian bush, and I love to get my hiking boots on and discover new wilderness.

host_about:
La Résidence Clignancourt, des appartements de charmes au cœur de Paris. Lassé des hôtels nichés dans les lieux touristiques et les pièges à touristes ? Envie de vivre comme un vrai parisien ? La Résidence Clignancourt vous offre un voyage qui vous permettra de vivre comme un français ; mélangé à la population locale avec ces bistros et ces restaurants typique. Quant à ceux qui cherchent le côté touristique, la Résidence Clignancourt se situe à cinq minutes à pieds de l’Eglise du Sacré Cœur qui offre une vue imprenable sur Paris. En plus des appartements dans le 18e arrondissement, vient s’ajouter un autre appartement situé dans le 15e arrondissement. 
Un quartier historique dans lequel vous vous perdrez dans le vieux Paris ; si vieux, que Place du Tertre se trouve le tout premier bistro de Paris. Un quartier avec une âme d’artiste puisque Place du Tertre, vous trouverez aussi tout plein d’artistes peintres mais aussi des galeries d’art et des magasins qui sentent bons le vieux Paris. La France, pays gastronomique, romantique, historique, venez voyager dans le temps, vous perdre de plaisir dans un endroit qui vous charmera.
Pour ce faire, la Résidence Clignancourt met à votre disposition cinq appartements de charme tout équipés. Chaque appartement est équipé d’une cuisine avec four à micro-ondes, d’une plaque chauffante, et de tous les ustensiles de cuisine nécessaires pour cuisiner et même, recevoir des amis. Bien sûr, chaque appartement est aussi équipé d’une salle de bain avec douche et toilettes et, de l’air conditionné pour certains et d’un sèche-cheveux, d’une télévision et du wifi gratuit. Draps, couette et serviettes de bain sont aussi mis à votre disposition, le papier toilette et les produits d’accueil. L’immeuble ne comporte pas en revanche d’ascenseur.
Nous vous proposons pour les familles nombreuses, l’appartement 1 et 6, qui peuvent recevoir jusqu’à six personnes.
Les appartements 2, 3 et 4 peuvent recevoir jusqu’à 4 personnes et l’appartement 5, deux personnes.
Et si vous cherchez un appartement de charme à l’ancienne avec les poutres apparentes et mansardé, ne cherchez plus, l’appartement 5 est fait pour vous. Une petite niche romantique sous les toits de Paris, dans l’un des quartiers les plus historique de la ville.

neighborhood_overview: Montparnasse, located on the south side of Paris on the left bank of the Seine, has a rich artistic legacy. The neighborhood was the home of thousands of artists and writers, many of whom were expatriates, during the 1920s and 1930s, the postwar period referred to as Les Années Folles. Today the area is far more upscale in nature, with boutique hotels and gourmet grocery stores. The lively dining scene includes both French fare and international cuisine, and there are chic cocktail bars throughout the neighborhood. You can also dine at La Closerie Des Lilas, one of Ernest Hemingway's old watering holes. Both the Paris Observatory and the Cartier Foundation for Contemporary Art are located in Montparnasse, and the ghoulish but fascinating Paris Catacombs lie at its southern border. The neighborhood is served by Paris's 4, 6, and 13 Metro lines.

It's a popular meeting place for Parisians and tourists alike, who come here in search of the authenticity of a Paris that's both traditional and modern. The cobblestones that cover the floor add to its old-world charm, while the outdoor stalls of merchants and florists add a touch of color and life. - Sanitise their mobile phones

host_about:
Je suis gestionnaire de propriétés privées en location de courte & moyenne durée depuis 2016 à Paris, sur la côte basque et la côte d'azur.. 

Passionnée, curieuse, gourmande, énergique...des mots qui me décrivent à la perfection!

Mes passions: 
La culture & l'Art. Mon précédent métier d'Agent d'Artistes m'a permis d'admirer des trésors inestimables, de découvrir une richesse incomparable dans le domaine de la création en France.

La cuisine. Je dois cette passion pour à ma grand mère. J'ai même eu ma chance dans l'émission Un dîner presque parfait en 2014 ;-). Aujourd'hui c'est avec mes filles que je passe du temps aux fourneaux. Le bonheur!

Le sport. Le jogging, comment dire? C'est mon défouloir! Surtout le long de l'Océan à Anglet!

Les sorties. J'aime Paris pour ça! Théâtre, expositions, concerts, spectacles, restaurants, bars, balades. Les sorties sont à couper le souffle à Paris tellement le choix est vaste. Il en existe pour tout le monde. Amoureux, célibataire, papi et mamie, enfants, animaux, bref, impossible de s'ennuyer! 
J'adore le quartier Saint Germain-des-prés, ses terrasses, ses galeries, ses boutiques, ses librairies, son histoire. 
J'adore aussi me balader à Montmartre, quartier le plus visité de Paris. La butte Montmartre est célèbre pour sa Basilique du Sacré Cœur et sa vue panoramique sur Paris. C'est aussi un quartier gastronomique et culturel au charme authentique, parsemé d'escaliers et de vieux lampadaires. Prenez le petit train de Montmartre depuis la place Blanche. C'est très sympa à faire en famille.

Chers voyageurs, sachez que vous êtes les bienvenus, à Paris, sur la Côte Basque ou en région PACA. Vous serez accueillis avec soin par moi même ou par mon équipe. Tout dépend où je me trouve ;-).

Les logements que je propose à la location saisonnière sont tous très bien équipés pour un confort optimal. C'est très important pour moi que vous gardiez un bon souvenir de vos vacances ou séjours professionnels.

Je vous souhaite un très beau moment, chez nous.

Delphine Thomas
SAS Thomas Real Estate

host_about:
Bonjour !

Nous sommes français-e-s et nous vivons à Paris depuis 15 ans. 
Marie est psychologue et Michael est chef de projet en informatique.
Nous aimons tout particulièrement notre ville pour toute la richesse culturelle et la beauté qu'elle propose.

Nous nous intéressons à tout ce qui est culturel, que ce soit la littérature, le théâtre, le cinéma, les expositions en tout genre, la visite de musées, la découvertes de quartiers ou d'endroits insolites. 
Nous avons nous même un appartement en location à Paris pour faire découvrir cette ville aux voyageur/se-s.

Nous adorons rencontrer de nouvelles personnes, apprendre l'histoire de leur pays et découvrir la gastronomie locale.

Voici quelques endroits que nous avons particulièrement appréciés :
- Les Highlands en Ecosse (et la rencontre de Nessie !)
- L'île de Sainte-Marie à Madagascar (et la rencontre avec les lémuriens)
- L'île de Guernesey (et la visite de la maison de Victor Hugo)
- Londres (et son ambiance british, et Camden town !)
- L'Irlande (et ses contrées féériques et en particulier la ville de Kinsale)
- Chicago (et son ambiance cabaret)
- Montréal (et son art de vivre)
- NYC (l'indescriptible ville qui ne dort jamais)
- L'île Maurice (et sa ville typique de Mahebourg)
- L'île de la Réunion (et son paysage lunaire)
- La Norvège (et sa beauté sauvage)
- Les îles Grecques (et la douceur de vivre, la beauté et l'accueil de la Grèce)

A très bientôt.
M&M's

neighborhood_overview:
The rue Saint-Honoré is a street in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, France.

It is named after the collegial Saint-Honoré church situated in ancient times within the cloisters of Saint-Honoré.

The street, on which are located a number of museums and upscale boutiques, is near the Jardin des Tuileries and the Saint-Honoré market. Like many streets in the heart of Paris, the rue Saint-Honoré, as it is now known, was laid out as early as the Middle Ages or before.

The street, at one time, continued beyond the former city walls into what was the faubourg (from Latin foris burgem, an area "outside the city"). This continuation was eventually named the rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré.

* Air House *:
Located in the Parc de Belleville, this small museum is dedicated to the quality of the air and the environment. It is an interesting educational place for families and science lovers.



# Monuments

* Église Saint-Jean-Baptiste de Belleville *:
A beautiful 19th century neo-Gothic church located near the Metro Station Jourdain It's notable for its architecture and bright interior.

* Rue Dénoyez *:
Although not a traditional landmark, this street is famous for its murals and artistic graffiti, part of Belleville's cultural and artistic heritage.



# Parks and Green Spaces

* Parc des Buttes-Chaumont *:
Within walking distance, this park is one of the largest and most picturesque in Paris. It offers hills, lakes, caves and panoramic views of the city from the Sybil gazebo.

This park offers unobstructed views of Paris

Hip galleries. Boutique shops. Pastoral cafés. Canal St. Martin in the 10th Arrondissement is everything you’d expect from the French capital, but with more than its fair share of contemporary cool.
 
Standing opposite Oscar Niemeyer’s iconic French Communist Headquarters, Generator Paris is just a few steps from Canal Saint-Martin and Buttes-Chaumont Park, and only a 15-minute stroll from Gare du Nord train station. With a welcoming mix of cinematic design, rich colours, a sparkling reception and several unique social spaces to suit your mood, you’ll feel like you’re on the set of a Parisian art-house movie.

On the ground floor of our Paris hotel, you'll find Café Fabien with its canteen and conservatory overlooking the garden. A curved staircase leads down to the vaulted ceilings of Le Club, inspired by the Paris Metro. Head up to the 9th floor to discover Khayma Rooftop, with a canopy, bar and awe-inspiring views of Sacré-Cœur and Montmartre. Our Paris property represents the very best of the city, all under one roof.

----------------------

Des galeries d'art mondaines aux boutiques indépendantes en passant par les cafés romanesques, le canal Saint-Martin dans le 10ème arrondissement est un concentré du charme parisien qui attire les habitants les plus branchés.

Generator Paris est situé en face du siège du Parti communiste français imaginé par l'architecte brésilien Oscar Niemeyer. L'hostel se trouve à quelques pas du canal Saint-Martin et du parc des Buttes-Chaumont et seulement à 15 minutes à pied de la gare du Nord. Plongez dans l'univers enivrant et électrique de cet hostel où les œuvres d'art accrochées aux murs vous donneront l'illusion d'être sur le tournage d'un film d'art parisien.

Au rez-de-chaussée se trouve la cantine du Café Fabien et sa véranda avec vue sur le jardin. Un escalier en colimaçon mène vers Le Club et ses voûtes inspirées du métro parisien. Montez au 9ème étage et découvrez Khayma Rooftop Bar et sa vue imprenable sur le Sacré-Cœur et Montmartre. Venez vivre une expérience typiquement parisienne dans notre hostel !

Welcome to Paris, the city of love and light! During your stay, you will be delighted to discover many points of interest near your accommodation.

- The church of Sainte-Marie-Madeleine is an architectural gem located in the Madeleine district. This impressive neoclassical church is a real masterpiece and definitely worth a visit.

- The Tuileries Gardens, located between the Louvre Museum and Place de la Concorde, offer an ideal relaxation area for a peaceful walk. Guests can enjoy its beautiful flower beds, fountains, and statues.

- The Musée du Parfum, located in the Opera district, will allow you to discover the enchanting world of fragrances. You can learn about the history of the fragrance and even create your own personalized fragrance.

- Le Jeu de Paume is a contemporary art museum located in the gardens of the Tuileries. It features temporary exhibitions of visual art, photography, and cinema, offering a unique cultural experience.

- Sanitise their mobile phones

The 16th arrondissement is also home to Roland Garros, host of the French Open tennis tournament. This arrondissement is slow-paced and best for ambling about; discovering places like le Palais du Trocadéro or Jardin d’Acclimitation, home to the world’s oldest operating amusement park. This arrondissement is also where you will find the Louis Vuitton Foundation and Bois de Boulogne.
host_about:
Greetings from the Veeve team!


Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods. Thanks to our fully managed service, when you stay in a Veeve property you can benefit from the spaciousness, personal style and relaxed feel of a home – but with all the amenities of a hotel.


Once a booking is confirmed our Customer Service team will become your main point of contact and get in touch with you to organise your arrival at the property (including airport transfers, upon request); after which our on-the-ground management team will look after all aspects of your stay, with in-stay support available to help with any queries.


We have strict cleanliness guidelines for our cleaners and all staff who enter our properties and have reinforced existing cleaning procedures in line with official WHO, British and French government guidance.


As always, our team ensure that all properties are cleaned to a professional standard before and after each stay, with increased focus on touch-point cleaning (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.).

 All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate

host_about:
Greetings from the Veeve team!


Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods. Thanks to our fully managed service, when you stay in a Veeve property you can benefit from the spaciousness, personal style and relaxed feel of a home – but with all the amenities of a hotel.


Once a booking is confirmed our Customer Service team will become your main point of contact and get in touch with you to organise your arrival at the property (including airport transfers, upon request); after which our on-the-ground management team will look after all aspects of your stay, with in-stay support available to help with any queries.


We have strict cleanliness guidelines for our cleaners and all staff who enter our properties and have reinforced existing cleaning procedures in line with official WHO, British and French government guidance.


As always, our team ensure that all properties are cleaned to a professional standard before and after each stay, with increased focus on touch-point cleaning (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.).

 All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate
- Wash and disinfect work shoes


We might be able to arrange for property viewings, upon request, for stays of over 28 nights. 

Please be aware once a booking is confirmed you will be required to complete a Rental Agreement and also  ID verification via our partners Superhog. This is mandatory for all our stays and in accordance to short lets requirements with Veeve.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be sure to answer you promptly.

The good news is that many of these new destinations have been re-purposed from former industrial buildings, putting a fresh modern face on a neglected area.

Originally an industrial suburb, the 13th arrondissement has undergone a sea change since it was annexed by Paris in 1860. Woods, fields and mills once stood where today there are streets and buildings. In the 14th century, the area became Paris’s manufacturing hub because of the presence of water from the Bièvre river, which then ran through the southern part of the capital. Shoemakers, laundry workers, tanners, weavers and dyers modified the river’s course to develop their activities, and contributed to Paris’s industrial progress.

The rue Saint-Honoré is a street in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, France.

It is named after the collegial Saint-Honoré church situated in ancient times within the cloisters of Saint-Honoré.

The street, on which are located a number of museums and upscale boutiques, is near the Jardin des Tuileries and the Saint-Honoré market. Like many streets in the heart of Paris, the rue Saint-Honoré, as it is now known, was laid out as early as the Middle Ages or before.

The street, at one time, continued beyond the former city walls into what was the faubourg (from Latin foris burgem, an area "outside the city"). This continuation was eventually named the rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré.

Je suis gestionnaire de propriétés privées en location de courte & moyenne durée depuis 2016 à Paris, sur la côte basque et la côte d'azur.. 

Passionnée, curieuse, gourmande, énergique...des mots qui me décrivent à la perfection!

Mes passions: 
La culture & l'Art. Mon précédent métier d'Agent d'Artistes m'a permis d'admirer des trésors inestimables, de découvrir une richesse incomparable dans le domaine de la création en France.

La cuisine. Je dois cette passion pour à ma grand mère. J'ai même eu ma chance dans l'émission Un dîner presque parfait en 2014 ;-). Aujourd'hui c'est avec mes filles que je passe du temps aux fourneaux. Le bonheur!

Le sport. Le jogging, comment dire? C'est mon défouloir! Surtout le long de l'Océan à Anglet!

Les sorties. J'aime Paris pour ça! Théâtre, expositions, concerts, spectacles, restaurants, bars, balades. Les sorties sont à couper le souffle à Paris tellement le choix est vaste. Il en existe pour tout le monde. Amoureux, célibataire, papi et mamie, enfants, animaux, bref, impossible de s'ennuyer! 
J'adore le quartier Saint Germain-des-prés, ses terrasses, ses galeries, ses boutiques, ses librairies, son histoire. 
J'adore aussi me balader à Montmartre, quartier le plus visité de Paris. La butte Montmartre est célèbre pour sa Basilique du Sacré Cœur et sa vue panoramique sur Paris. C'est aussi un quartier gastronomique et culturel au charme authentique, parsemé d'escaliers et de vieux lampadaires. Prenez le petit train de Montmartre depuis la place Blanche. C'est très sympa à faire en famille.

Chers voyageurs, sachez que vous êtes les bienvenus, à Paris, sur la Côte Basque ou en région PACA. Vous serez accueillis avec soin par moi même ou par mon équipe. Tout dépend où je me trouve ;-).

Les logements que je propose à la location saisonnière sont tous très bien équipés pour un confort optimal. C'est très important pour moi que vous gardiez un bon souvenir de vos vacances ou séjours professionnels.

Je vous souhaite un très beau moment, chez nous.

Delphine Thomas

host_about:
Bonjour je m' appelle Delphine, je vis dans mon appartement avec mon petit garçon.

L'appartement donne sur un jardin arboré, extrêmement calme et lumineux avec de grandes baies vitrées, il a entièrement été refait à neuf, avec un beau parquet. Il comporte 2 grandes portes coulissantes, ce qui permet l'habitation d'être un mono-espace (tout ouvert pour une personne seule ou en couple) ou portes fermées le soir pour les 2 chambres).

Notre appartement est conçu pour 3, mais nous avons 2 couchages supplémentaires d'appoints. 

L' appartement est composé d'une entrée avec un grand placard et un dressing, d'un beau salon salle à mangé, d'une cuisine ouverte dotée d'un petit bar, d'une chambre parentales avec un grand lit double (queen size) et de la salle de bain/buanderie, toilettes séparées. Une chambre d'enfant avec mezzanine (lit simple) et les 2 couchages d'appoints (un futon double à déplier) 

L'appartement est particulièrement bien situé, à 2 pas de La Bastille, de la Gare de Lyon et du Quartier Latin.
Très bien desservi par 4 stations de métro, le M° Ledru Rollin-(ligne 8) le plus proche, à moins de 5min. Puis à moins de 10 mins M° Charonne (ligne 9), M° Bastille (ligne 1 et 5)  et La Gare de Lyon (ligne 1 et le RER A et RER D) ainsi que les stations de bus : le 86, 76, 46, 56 et le 91.

Il se situe dans un quartier très animé, de restaurants, bars, boutiques, cinémas, théâtre et le Marché tous les matins à l'exception du lundi, à quelques pas de la maison.

Nous aimons la convivialité qui prend une place importante dans notre vie. L'appartement en est le reflet. Nous y sommes très heureux.

neighborhood_overview: Situated next to the Arc de Triomphe, the 17th arrondissement is slightly off the beaten track. However, if you’d like to see some of the finest architecture in Paris, then look no further. This arrondissement, without any major sites, is a story of two tales; to north-eastern end of the 17th, more commonly known as Batignolles, you’ll find a relaxed bohemian atmosphere with a large variety of bars and eateries. In contrast, the south-western side of the 17th feels like an extension of the Champs Élysées with a large selection of midrange to high-end shops. host_about:
Greetings from the Veeve team!


Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017. Our rental homes are predominantly privately-owned, lived-in homes in vibrant neighbourhoods. Thanks to our fully managed service, when you stay in a Veeve property you can benefit from the spaciousness, personal style and relaxed feel of a home – but with all the amenities of a hotel.


Once a booking is confirmed our Customer Service team will become your main point of contact and get in touch with you to organise your arrival at the property (including airport transfers, upon request); after which our on-the-ground management team will look after all aspects of your stay, with in-stay support available to help with any queries.


We have strict cleanliness guidelines for our cleaners and all staff who enter our properties and have reinforced existing cleaning procedures in line with official WHO, British and French government guidance.


As always, our team ensure that all properties are cleaned to a professional standard before and after each stay, with increased focus on touch-point cleaning (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.).

 All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate
- Wash and disinfect work shoes


We might be able to arrange for property viewings, upon request, for stays of over 28 nights.

neighborhood_overview:
The Beaujolais is a superbly located apartment, literally two blocks from the Eiffel Tower, in the historic and architecturally stunning 7th arrondissement on the Left Bank. The 7th is also home to such must-see Parisian sites as the Musée D’Orsay, Rodin Museum, Napoleon's Tomb and Invalides, the Army Museum and the exceptional Le Bon Marche department store.

Just around the corner from the world-famous Rue Cler street market, the Beaujolais is ideal for foodies. Open daily, you can shop like a local at fresh produce stalls and speciality food shops, or just watch the world go by from one of the neighbourhood’s numerous cafes and Michelin-starred restaurants.

The Seine is also close by, ideal for a riverside stroll or catching a river cruise – one of the best ways to see the city’s bridges and monuments. Getting around wider Paris is also easy, with the Pont de l'Alma and Ecole Militaire Metro stations nearby.

host_about:
Hip galleries. Boutique shops. Pastoral cafés. Canal St. Martin in the 10th Arrondissement is everything you’d expect from the French capital, but with more than its fair share of contemporary cool.
 
Standing opposite Oscar Niemeyer’s iconic French Communist Headquarters, Generator Paris is just a few steps from Canal Saint-Martin and Buttes-Chaumont Park, and only a 15-minute stroll from Gare du Nord train station. With a welcoming mix of cinematic design, rich colours, a sparkling reception and several unique social spaces to suit your mood, you’ll feel like you’re on the set of a Parisian art-house movie.

On the ground floor of our Paris hotel, you'll find Café Fabien with its canteen and conservatory overlooking the garden. A curved staircase leads down to the vaulted ceilings of Le Club, inspired by the Paris Metro. Head up to the 9th floor to discover Khayma Rooftop, with a canopy, bar and awe-inspiring views of Sacré-Cœur and Montmartre. Our Paris property represents the very best of the city, all under one roof.

----------------------

Des galeries d'art mondaines aux boutiques indépendantes en passant par les cafés romanesques, le canal Saint-Martin dans le 10ème arrondissement est un concentré du charme parisien qui attire les habitants les plus branchés.

Generator Paris est situé en face du siège du Parti communiste français imaginé par l'architecte brésilien Oscar Niemeyer. L'hostel se trouve à quelques pas du canal Saint-Martin et du parc des Buttes-Chaumont et seulement à 15 minutes à pied de la gare du Nord. Plongez dans l'univers enivrant et électrique de cet hostel où les œuvres d'art accrochées aux murs vous donneront l'illusion d'être sur le tournage d'un film d'art parisien.

Au rez-de-chaussée se trouve la cantine du Café Fabien et sa véranda avec vue sur le jardin. Un escalier en colimaçon mène vers Le Club et ses voûtes inspirées du métro parisien. Montez au 9ème étage et découvrez Khayma Rooftop Bar et sa vue imprenable sur le Sacré-Cœur et Montmartre. Venez vivre une expérience typiquement parisienne dans notre hostel !

Veeve manage the largest collection of homes to rent for short stays in London since 2011, launching in Paris in 2017.  All staff who enter properties will follow the below procedures:
 

- Carry and regularly use alcohol-based hand rub
- Sanitise their mobile phones 
- Focus extra attention when cleaning key touch-point areas (door handles, kitchen surfaces, kettles, taps etc.)
- Wear protective gear where appropriate
- Wash and disinfect work shoes


We might be able to arrange for property viewings, upon request, for stays of over 28 nights. 

Please be aware once a booking is confirmed you will be required to complete a Rental Agreement and also  ID verification via our partners Superhog. This is mandatory for all our stays and in accordance to short lets requirements with Veeve.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be sure to answer you promptly.
